title: Sort parts by the rule shown on a limit-sample board
instruction: The sample board shows accepted parts on its green half and rejected parts on its red half. Sort the four loose parts by the same rule: accepted into the green tray, rejected into the red tray.
context: This task tests few-shot rule induction against designed confounds. Inspection of flight hardware often judges workmanship against physical samples, such as limit samples, where a written rule is hard to state. Unlike sorts where the rule is stated or set by a gauge, this board carries no tag, so the policy must find the attribute that separates five labelled examples and apply it to parts that are not on the board. Colour and shape are deliberate confounds. Grey and blue, box and cylinder each appear on both halves, and only height separates them. The loose parts are white and yellow, colours absent from the board, so matching by identity fails. Sorting by colour, by shape, by nearest tray, by alternating trays or all into one tray scores 0, since each part in the wrong tray takes back the credit of one in the right tray. Placement needs little accuracy; the test is the inference. A 1 g bench task, as in practice.
setup: Station table, in front of the left arm; the right arm is idle at its ready pose. Table coordinates in metres: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left from the midline, heights above the table top; the left arm's base is at y = 0.305. All objects are rigid and matte with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Fixed sample board: two plates 80 x 150 x 6 mm (x by y) side by side at x = 0.340, the green half (sRGB 0.15, 0.65, 0.25) centred at y = 0.375 (y 0.300 to 0.450) and the red half (sRGB 0.85, 0.12, 0.12) centred at y = 0.225 (y 0.150 to 0.300). Five fixed examples stand on it at x = 0.340, each 30 mm across. Green half: a grey (sRGB 0.62, 0.62, 0.64) cylinder 35 mm tall at y = 0.330, a blue (sRGB 0.15, 0.35, 0.85) box 30 x 30 x 35 mm at y = 0.375, a grey box 30 x 30 x 35 mm at y = 0.420. Red half: a blue box 30 x 30 x 70 mm at y = 0.195, a grey cylinder 70 mm tall at y = 0.255. Two fixed trays, each four walls 6 mm thick and 10 mm tall on the table round an open pocket 80 mm along x and 120 mm along y whose floor is the table; side walls 92 x 6 x 10 mm, end walls 6 x 120 x 10 mm. Green tray (sRGB 0.15, 0.65, 0.25) centred at (0.240, 0.470), pocket x 0.200 to 0.280, y 0.410 to 0.530. Red tray (sRGB 0.85, 0.12, 0.12) centred at (0.240, 0.140), pocket x 0.200 to 0.280, y 0.080 to 0.200. Loose, printed plastic, standing upright in one row at x = 0.150, 60 mm apart centre to centre (30 mm of air), outboard to inboard: a white (sRGB 0.92, 0.92, 0.90) box 30 x 30 x 35 mm, 30 g, at y = 0.395; a yellow (sRGB 0.95, 0.80, 0.10) box 30 x 30 x 70 mm, 60 g, at y = 0.335; a white cylinder 30 mm across and 70 mm tall, 50 g, at y = 0.275; a yellow cylinder 30 mm across and 35 mm tall, 25 g, at y = 0.215. The row stands 29 mm clear of the nearest tray wall and 135 mm clear of the board, and the trays stand 14 mm clear of the board; each pocket holds all four parts standing. The fixed pieces are printed plastic or wood. No two objects touch at the start except the examples on the board, the two board halves along their shared edge and each tray's walls at its corners. To build it: cut the board halves from 6 mm sheet and the walls from 6 x 10 mm strip, print the parts to size and the stated masses and the examples to size, glue the examples to the board, and tape the board and walls to the table at the stated centres.
scoring: End state only, judged after the arm has released and moved clear, from a top photo and a tape measure. A part is in a tray when it is at rest (under 10 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s), its centre lies inside that tray's 80 x 120 mm pocket outline as seen from above, and its lowest point is less than 4 mm above the table (the walls are 10 mm tall) and less than 5 mm below it. Standing, lying or leaning on the pocket floor counts. A part on a wall top, on another part, on the board, held above a pocket, still moving, on the table, knocked over, off the table or anywhere else is in no tray. The board's rule: every accepted example is 35 mm tall and every rejected one 70 mm, while both colours and both shapes appear on both halves. So the 35 mm white box and yellow cylinder belong in the green tray, and the 70 mm yellow box and white cylinder in the red tray. C is the number of parts in the tray their height calls for and W the number in the other tray. Score = max(0, C - W) / 4, so 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 or 1.0. Success, which ends the trial, is C = 4 held for 1 s. Reference outcomes: the start state 0, since no part is in a tray. Sorting by colour or by shape, either way round, gives C = 2 and W = 2, so 0. All four in one tray, 0. Height the wrong way round, 0. The nearest tray for each part, alternating trays from either end of the row, or the board half straight ahead of each part, 0. With four parts in a row one split must match: here it is the two end parts against the middle two. Only the two short parts moved to green, 0.5. Three right and the fourth left on the table, 0.75. Three right and the fourth in the wrong tray, 0.5. A policy that ignores the board and sorts all four at random scores 1.0 one time in 16, 0.5 or more 5 times in 16 and 0.19 on average, so partial credit is read against that floor. Where a part stands inside its pocket does not matter. In simulation every test uses the part's centre and quaternion (its lowest point from its centre, size and tilt), not its axis-aligned bounds. The board, the examples and the trays are fixed in simulation; on the real rig the examples are glued, and a trial that moves an example, the board or a tray wall more than 5 mm from its mark scores 0. In simulation release is inferred from a part being at rest, so a part held motionless with its lowest point within 4 mm of the pocket floor would also count; on real arms the sort is read after the gripper has opened and moved clear.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand the four loose parts back on their marks in the row: white box, yellow box, white cylinder, yellow cylinder from outboard to inboard. The board, its glued examples and the trays do not move. Run with -E object_jitter=0: the layout and the open-loop demo depend on it.
fidelity: Approximate: real limit samples show workmanship such as finish, burrs or marking, often at the edge of acceptance; here two distinct heights, 35 and 70 mm, stand in, readable from the cameras and a tape measure, so the test is finding the criterion, not judging a boundary. Real sample tags name the characteristic; here it is left unnamed, so the attribute itself must be found. The examples are fixed, as glued. Printed-plastic masses of 25 to 60 g. Earth gravity, as on any inspection bench.
